title: syntomic characterize
conclusions: If f syntomic, any restriction U→V with f(U)⊆V syntomic
equivalent_conditions: All compatible affine opens induce syntomic ring maps
There exist open coverings V_j of S and U_i of f^{-1}(V_j) with all U_i→V_j syntomic
These coverings can be chosen affine and associated ring maps syntomic
standalone_statement_latex:
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item The morphism $f$ is syntomic.
\item For every affine opens $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$
with $f(U) \subset V$ the ring map
$\mathcal{O}_S(V) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U)$ is syntomic.
\item There exists an open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$
and open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such
that each of the morphisms $U_i \to V_j$, $j\in J, i\in I_j$
is syntomic.
\item There exists an affine open covering $S = \bigcup_{j \in J} V_j$
and affine open coverings $f^{-1}(V_j) = \bigcup_{i \in I_j} U_i$ such
that the ring map $\mathcal{O}_S(V_j) \to \mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$ is
syntomic, for all $j\in J, i\in I_j$.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if $f$ is syntomic then for
any open subschemes $U \subset X$, $V \subset S$ with $f(U) \subset V$
the restriction $f|_U : U \to V$ is syntomic.

title: composition syntomic
explicit_hypotheses: X→Y and Y→Z composable syntomic scheme morphisms
standalone_statement_latex: For syntomic morphisms of schemes \(X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}Z\), the composite \(g\circ f\) is syntomic.

title: base change syntomic
standalone_statement_latex: For any syntomic morphism of schemes \(f:X\to S\) and any morphism \(S'\to S\), the base change \(X\times_S S'\to S'\) is syntomic.

title: open immersion syntomic
explicit_hypotheses: U→X an open immersion of schemes
standalone_statement_latex: Every open immersion \(U\hookrightarrow X\) of schemes is syntomic.

title: syntomic locally finite presentation
standalone_statement_latex: Every syntomic morphism \(f:X\to S\) of schemes is locally of finite presentation.

title: syntomic flat
standalone_statement_latex: Every syntomic morphism \(f:X\to S\) of schemes is flat.

title: syntomic open
standalone_statement_latex: Every syntomic morphism \(f:X\to S\) of schemes is universally open.

title: local complete intersection
explicit_hypotheses: X scheme locally finite type over k
equivalent_conditions: X local complete intersection over k
Every x has an affine neighborhood Spec(R) with R a global complete intersection over k
For every x, O_{X,x} a complete intersection over k
standalone_statement_latex:
Let $k$ be a field.
Let $X$ be a scheme locally of finite type over $k$.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ is a local complete intersection over $k$,
\item for every $x \in X$ there exists an affine open
$U = \Spec(R) \subset X$ neighbourhood of $x$
such that $R \cong k[x_1, \ldots, x_n]/(f_1, \ldots, f_c)$
is a global complete intersection over $k$, and
\item for every $x \in X$ the local ring $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$
is a complete intersection over $k$.
\end{enumerate}

title: syntomic locally standard syntomic
equivalent_conditions: There exists an affine U⊆X containing x with f(U)⊆V such that U→V standard syntomic
f finite presentation at x; O_{S,s}→O_{X,x} flat; fibre local ring O_{X,x}/m_s O_{X,x} a complete intersection over κ(s)
standalone_statement_latex:
Let $f : X  \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $x \in X$ be a point
with image $s = f(x)$. Let $V \subset S$ be an affine open neighbourhood
of $s$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item The morphism $f$ is syntomic at $x$.
\item There exist an affine open $U \subset X$ with $x \in U$ and
$f(U) \subset V$ such that $f|_U : U \to V$ is standard syntomic.
\item The morphism $f$ is of finite presentation at $x$, the local ring map
$\mathcal{O}_{S, s} \to \mathcal{O}_{X, x}$
is flat and $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}/\mathfrak m_s \mathcal{O}_{X, x}$
is a complete intersection over $\kappa(s)$ (see
Algebra, Definition \ref{algebra-definition-lci-local-ring}).
\end{enumerate}

title: syntomic flat fibres
explicit_hypotheses: f:X→S flat and locally of finite presentation
Every scheme fibre X_s over κ(s) is a local complete intersection
standalone_statement_latex:
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
If $f$ is flat, locally of finite presentation, and all
fibres $X_s$ are local complete intersections, then $f$
is syntomic.

title: set points where fibres lci
explicit_hypotheses: T={x∈X: O_{X_{f(x)},x} complete intersection over κ(f(x))}
S'→S arbitrary, f':X'→S' its base change
conclusions: If f also flat and locally finite presentation, the syntomic locus is open and commutes with base change
standalone_statement_latex:
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Assume $f$ locally of finite type. Formation of the set
$$
T = \{x \in X \mid \mathcal{O}_{X_{f(x)}, x}
\text{ is a complete intersection over }\kappa(f(x))\}
$$
commutes with arbitrary base change:
For any morphism $g : S' \to S$, consider
the base change $f' : X' \to S'$ of $f$ and the
projection $g' : X' \to X$. Then the corresponding
set $T'$ for the morphism $f'$ is equal to $T' = (g')^{-1}(T)$.
In particular, if $f$ is assumed flat, and locally of finite
presentation then the same holds for the open set of points
where $f$ is syntomic.

title: standard syntomic relative dimension
explicit_hypotheses: A=R[x_1,...,x_n]/(f_1,...,f_c) a relative global complete intersection
standalone_statement_latex:
Let $R$ be a ring.
Let $R \to A = R[x_1, \ldots, x_n]/(f_1, \ldots, f_c)$ be a relative
global complete intersection. Set $S = \Spec(R)$ and
$X = \Spec(A)$. Consider the morphism
$f : X \to S$ associated to the ring map $R \to A$.
The function $x \mapsto \dim_x(X_{f(x)})$ is constant with value $n - c$.
unresolved_context: Relative global complete intersection imposes regular-sequence conditions, not merely an arbitrary presentation

title: syntomic relative dimension
standalone_statement_latex: For a syntomic morphism of schemes \(f:X\to S\), the fibre dimension function \(x\mapsto\dim_x(X_{f(x)})\) is locally constant on \(X\).

title: syntomic permanence
explicit_hypotheses: X→Y→S commuting triangle of scheme morphisms with f:X→Y, p:X→S, q:Y→S and p=q∘f
standalone_statement_latex: Let \(X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{q}S\) be morphisms of schemes, and write \(p=q\circ f:X\to S\). If \(f\) is surjective and syntomic, \(p\) is syntomic, and \(q\) is locally of finite presentation, then \(q\) is syntomic.
